es.summary: Se cargó en un endpoint Windows el driver de kernel de Process Hacker (kprocesshacker.sys) o un driver con uno de sus imphash conocidos. Esto da acceso a nivel de kernel a una herramienta capaz de terminar procesos protegidos.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de carga de driver (Sysmon EventID 6) cuyo ImageLoaded termina en \kprocesshacker.sys, o cuyo campo Hashes contiene uno de cuatro IMPHASH asociados al driver de Process Hacker, aunque el archivo esté renombrado.
es.why_it_matters: Process Hacker es una utilidad legítima, pero su driver permite manipular o terminar procesos que el usuario no podría tocar, como agentes AV/EDR. Instalar un driver como servicio corresponde a ATT&CK T1543 (crear o modificar procesos del sistema), usado para persistencia y escalamiento de privilegios.
triage_steps: Revise ImageLoaded: una ruta como C:\Program Files\Process Hacker 2\ es esperable; un nombre distinto en Temp, Users\Public o ProgramData con IMPHASH coincidente sugiere un driver renombrado.
Valide Hashes, Signed, Signature y SignatureStatus; compare el hash con el inventario de software aprobado de la organización.
Busque en el mismo host, +/- 15 minutos, la creación de procesos (ProcessHacker.exe u otro ejecutable) que extrajo o cargó el driver, e identifique al usuario y su proceso padre.
Revise la creación de servicios (System 7045, Sysmon 13 bajo HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services) para ver el nombre del servicio y la ruta del driver.
Verifique si después se detuvieron o terminaron procesos del AV/EDR, o si hubo acceso a LSASS (Sysmon 10) desde el mismo proceso.
Consulte con el usuario o su responsable si la herramienta fue usada para una tarea administrativa autorizada.
Busque alertas previas del host y del usuario, y otros hosts con el mismo hash del driver.
false_positives: Desarrolladores o administradores que usan Process Hacker o System Informer para depurar o diagnosticar el sistema.
Equipos de soporte técnico que ejecutan la herramienta desde un kit portátil aprobado durante un análisis de rendimiento.
response_steps: Confirme con el usuario y el dueño del activo si el uso estaba autorizado; si lo estaba, documéntelo y considere una excepción por host y hash.
Si no está autorizado, aísle el endpoint desde el EDR y verifique que los agentes de seguridad sigan en ejecución.
Una vez confirmada la actividad maliciosa, preserve el driver y el ejecutable, y luego deshabilite y elimine el servicio asociado.
Revise credenciales del usuario implicado, restablézcalas si hubo acceso a LSASS y busque movimiento lateral desde el host.
Bloquee el hash del driver mediante políticas de control de aplicaciones o la lista de drivers vulnerables bloqueados.
es.severity_rationale: Es alta porque un driver de kernel capaz de terminar herramientas de seguridad suele preceder a ataques graves, aunque existe uso administrativo legítimo que debe descartarse.

en.summary: The Process Hacker kernel driver (kprocesshacker.sys), or a driver matching one of its known imphashes, was loaded on a Windows endpoint. This gives a tool that can kill protected processes access at kernel level.
en.what_it_detects: Driver load events (Sysmon EventID 6) where ImageLoaded ends with \kprocesshacker.sys, or where the Hashes field contains one of four IMPHASH values tied to the Process Hacker driver, even when the file is renamed.
en.why_it_matters: Process Hacker is a legitimate utility, but its driver can tamper with or kill processes a user normally cannot touch, such as AV/EDR agents. Installing a driver as a service maps to ATT&CK T1543 (create or modify system process), used for persistence and privilege escalation.
triage_steps: Check ImageLoaded: a path like C:\Program Files\Process Hacker 2\ is expected. A different filename in Temp, Users\Public or ProgramData with a matching IMPHASH suggests a renamed driver.
Validate Hashes, Signed, Signature and SignatureStatus, and compare the hash against your approved software inventory.
On the same host within +/- 15 minutes, find the process creation (ProcessHacker.exe or another binary) that dropped or loaded the driver, plus its user and parent process.
Review service creation (System 7045, Sysmon 13 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services) for the service name and driver path.
Check whether AV/EDR processes were stopped or killed afterwards, or whether the same process accessed LSASS (Sysmon 10).
Ask the user or their manager whether the tool was used for an authorized administrative task.
Look for earlier alerts for the host and user, and for other hosts with the same driver hash.
false_positives: Developers or administrators using Process Hacker or System Informer for debugging or system diagnostics.
Help desk staff running the tool from an approved portable toolkit during performance troubleshooting.
response_steps: Confirm with the user and asset owner whether the use was authorized. If it was, document it and consider a host-and-hash scoped exception.
If it was not authorized, isolate the endpoint through the EDR and check that the security agents are still running.
Once you confirm malicious activity, preserve the driver and the executable, then disable and remove the related service.
Review the involved user's credentials, reset them if LSASS was accessed, and hunt for lateral movement from the host.
Block the driver hash with application control policies or the vulnerable driver blocklist.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because a kernel driver that can kill security tools often comes before serious attacks, though you still need to rule out legitimate admin use.

positive.description: Process Hacker driver loaded from its default install directory.
Renamed driver in a public folder whose imphash matches the Process Hacker driver.

negative.description: Sysinternals Process Explorer driver load, a similar tool but different filename and imphash.
Backup copy whose name only contains kprocesshacker.sys without ending in it, and whose imphash does not match.
